statute.name: Wis. Admin. Code ch. DCF 150; Wis. Stat. §§ 49.22(9), 767.511

incomeDefinition: Monthly income available for child support = annual gross income (or income modified for business expenses) + income imputed based on earning capacity + income imputed when little information is known + income imputed from assets, divided by 12 (DCF 150.02(21), 150.03(1)). Gross income includes wages, interest and investment income, Social Security disability and old-age benefits, income-replacing workers' compensation, unemployment insurance, voluntary deferred compensation and employee contributions to benefit or retirement plans, veterans disability and military allowances, certain undistributed business income, and all other income, but excludes child support, foster care and kinship care payments, public assistance, food stamps, SSI and other public assistance (DCF 150.02(13)). No taxes are deducted.
modelText: Support = 17% (1 child), 25% (2), 29% (3), 31% (4), 34% (5+) of the payer's monthly income available for child support (DCF 150.035(2)). For high-income payers the full income is considered, but the court may apply reduced marginal percentages on income from $7,000 to $12,500/month (14/20/23/25/27%) and above $12,500/month (10/15/17/19/20%) (DCF 150.04(5)). Low-income payers may be ordered under Appendix C.
sharedText: Shared-placement formula applies when both parents have court-ordered placement of at least 25% or 92 days a year; each parent's percentage amount is multiplied by 150% and by the other parent's share of time, then offset; the payer pays the lesser of the result or the standard percentage amount (DCF 150.035(1)). The rule was renumbered from DCF 150.04(2) to DCF 150.035(1) effective December 1, 2021.
addOnsText: Child care is a 'variable cost' (DCF 150.02(29)); in shared placement the court assigns variable costs in proportion to each parent's share of physical placement (DCF 150.035(1)(b)6). Otherwise it is covered by the percentage or by deviation. The court assigns responsibility for the child's health expenses (DCF 150.05, Wis. Stat. § 767.513). Private insurance is reasonable in cost if it does not exceed 10% of the insuring parent's monthly income available for child support; the non-insuring parent may be ordered to contribute up to 10% of his or her income, which may be built into the support amount (DCF 150.05(1)(b)). Medical support is ordered in addition to child support (DCF 150.05).
lowIncomeText: For payers with income between 75% and 150% of the federal poverty guidelines the court may use the Appendix C schedule (2026 version effective March 1, 2026: from $998.00 to $2,031.00 monthly income, e.g. 11.22% / $112 for one child at the lowest row); below the lowest level the court sets an amount fitting the payer's total economic circumstances (DCF 150.04(4)). DCF revises Appendix C every year from the federal poverty guidelines.

emancipation.text: The duty of support continues until the child turns 18, or 19 if the child is still enrolled in high school or working toward a high school equivalency (DCF, When Child Support Ends).

scheduleText: Each row gives the support for a monthly income available for child support 'up to' the stated amount (Appendix C heading 'Monthly Income Up To'). Use is discretionary: the court may apply it if the payer's total economic circumstances limit ability to pay (DCF 150.04(4)(a)).
aboveMaxText: At or above 150% of the federal poverty guidelines the standard percentages apply (DCF 150.04(4) note).

facts.text: Wisconsin's guideline uses gross income, not net income: no taxes are deducted (DCF 150.02(13), DCF 150.03(1)).
The 150% multiplier in shared placement accounts for household costs duplicated by both parents, such as a bedroom, clothes and personal items (note to DCF 150.035(1)(b)3).
Since January 1, 2024, daytime 'equivalent care' can count toward placement: two blocks of at least 6 hours with a meal equal one overnight (DCF 150.035(1)(ar)).
The low-income table (Appendix C) is revised every year from the federal poverty guidelines; the 2026 table took effect March 1, 2026 and the next one will take effect March 1, 2027.
Past-due support may be enforced up to 20 years after the youngest child turns 18 (DCF).
